newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to propose bill on compensatory time.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to propose bill on compensatory time.

text.p: The White House will propose legislation that would let workers trade overtime for compensatory time and would expand the law that guarantees workers the right to take unpaid leave during a family medical crisis, The Washington Post reported in Saturday editions.

The paper quoted administration sources as saying the president did not expect Congress to approve the bill, which would be attached to the Family and Medical Leave Act. But they said it would demonstrate his support for family-friendly policies during his re-election campaign.

The new Clinton proposal would expand the existing law to allow workers to take up to 24 hours of unpaid leave a year for dealing with such family duties as attending a child's school play or accompanying an elderly relative to the doctor.
The White House proposal would allow an employee to accumulate up to 80 hours of comp-time.
